Consequently, a single model comprising both the TES loop and the indoor coil is required, with refrigerant flow switching from the indoor coil for cooling or heating to the TES for recharge. To build such a model, a check valve model with a Boolean input was implemented in the in-house Modelica library [81]. In this model, a differential equation was implemented (Eq. (12)), where a target opening is set based on the Boolean input (i.e., if “true,” then the valve is fully opened “1”, else the valve is fully closed “0” ). The change in opening occurs over a short time constant (e.g., 0.5 seconds), and the refrigerant mass flow therefore changes in response to the available opening. To mimic an actual check valve, a minimum opening of 10-4% was assumed. The check valves placed before the component determine which refrigerant branch is open (depending on operating mode), while the valves placed after the component prevent backflow into the already sealed component. In cooling mode, both the BPHX and the indoor coil are on the low-pressure line, whereas in heating mode, they are on the high-pressure line (Figure 82). Figure 82: HP-TES system-level model with base and recharge operations in (a) cooling, and (b) heating modes Page 85 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park The cyclic HP-TES recharge and base HP model in cooling mode was implemented for the test case Test 4C (80°F/67°F) (Figure 83). Experimentally, no capacity degradation was observed in base operation compared to the rated AHRI Standard 210/240 (2017) A-Test 14.1 kW (4-ton) capacity. The cyclic HP-TES model showed excellent agreement in cooling capacity, TES recharge capacity, system input power, and compressor inlet and outlet pressures throughout the TES recharge process, with slight deviations in compressor suction and discharge conditions. These deviations are likely due to reversing valve leakage during the test, which may result in refrigerant charge re- distribution delays. Nonetheless, the two-operation HP-TES Modelica system-level model smoothly switched between modes and captured the HP-TES system transient behavior.
